body:
MEASURED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-24, Kobo Clara BW firmware 4.45.23792, against the
deployed server, on a probe book that held zero annotations at baseline.

## What was observed

A highlight that was **on no device snapshot** and is **`hidden=1` on the CWNG
server** was restored to the reader by a re-download, rendered on the page, and
marked `Hidden='false'` locally.

Annotation `789e11f0-6511-462e-9614-f465fef39592` (`Vivek `, created
2026-08-24T04:42:20Z during an earlier probe, CWNG row id 645, `hidden=1`):

    device snapshots t0, t1, t1b, t2, t4   row ABSENT   (5 consecutive pulls)
    after the re-download (t5)             row PRESENT  Hidden='false'
                                           SyncTime = 2026-08-24T22:37:48Z
                                                      (the re-download's sync)

It is drawn on the page, photographed alongside two live highlights, so this is
not a hidden-row artefact: the reader sees a highlight they no longer have.

## Where it came from, and where it did not

**Not from CWNG's writeback.** [OBSERVED] `config_kobo_two_way_annotation_sync`
is `0`; book 540's `kobo_annotation_book_state` is `authority_status='unseeded'`
with `current_etag` NULL; there are **zero** `annotation_device_state` rows for
this annotation. `cps/readingservices.py` contains no `hidden` handling at all.

**From upstream Kobo, through our proxy.** [OBSERVED in source]
`handle_annotations` at `cps/readingservices.py:468` documents and implements
exactly this: *"GET: proxied directly to Kobo."* The PATCH path captures locally
**and** proxies upstream, so every annotation the device ever authored on a
sideloaded book has also been stored in Kobo's cloud. On the authoritative fetch
that follows a re-download, Kobo returns the set **it** holds, and CWNG passes it
through unfiltered.

## Why this matters beyond one probe row

The proxy is transparent in both directions, so **Kobo's copy outranks both the
device's and CWNG's.** Any annotation the user deleted on the device, or that
CWNG has soft-deleted, is re-delivered whenever the device next fetches
authoritatively — and `F-0b66d7` already established that a device-side deletion
only reaches the server when a later annotation change in the **same book**
carries it out. A deletion that never found a carrier is still live in Kobo's
cloud, waiting for the next re-download.

Composed with `F-5ff379` (a `last_modified` bump de-downloads the book) and the
`mark_book_modified` call sites — ordinary metadata edits, cover changes, fetched
metadata, format conversion, not just the KEPUB repair task — the user-visible
sequence is:

    user deletes a highlight
      -> deletion finds no same-book carrier, never reaches Kobo   [F-0b66d7]
      -> anyone edits that book's metadata                          [OBSERVED]
      -> device drops its downloaded copy                           [OBSERVED]
      -> user reopens the book, it re-downloads                     [OBSERVED]
      -> the deleted highlight is back, drawn on the page           [OBSERVED]

## What this means for the two-way sync design

`notes/KOBO-TWO-WAY-ANNOTATION-SYNC-DESIGN.md` treats CWNG as the authority once
a book is seeded. This finding says the **unseeded** path is not inert: it is an
active resurrection channel we currently proxy verbatim. Seeding a book does not
retire it unless the seeded path also stops proxying the GET. Section 11 should
state which side wins when Kobo's set and CWNG's set disagree, because today the
answer is "Kobo, silently".

## Not established

- Why Kobo still held this row. Two candidates — the deletion never reached Kobo,
  or it reached Kobo and was ignored — need different fixes. Distinguishing them
  needs the full PATCH/GET bodies on the wire, which is precisely what the
  exchange capture on **#1816** records. This is a concrete argument for landing
  that instrument.
- Whether an authoritative fetch happens on any trigger other than a re-download.
- Whether a note (`Add Note`) resurrects the same way as a bare highlight.

## Side observation, same run

The book's reading progress read **2% Read** before the cycle and **1% Read**
after. Not investigated; recorded so a later session does not treat it as new.
title: A re-download resurrects deleted highlights, because CWNG proxies the Kobo annotations GET verbatim
